I checked the installed Starlette (.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/starlette/templating.py:84-90). On the installed version the directory branch falls back to `jinja2.select_autoescape()` at templating.py:95, which escapes by file extension only. Autoescape is a control against script injection (XSS), and it would then hold only by default for templates with an .html/.htm/.xml extension.

findings.problem: The diff removes the explicit `jinja2.Environment(loader=..., autoescape=True)` + `Jinja2Templates(env=_jinja_env)` construction and replaces it with `Jinja2Templates(directory=str(TEMPLATES_DIR), autoescape=True)`. This is a direct revert of commit e11187e ('fix: use preconfigured jinja2.Environment for autoescape'), whose own message states: 'Starlette removed the **env_options passthrough in Jinja2Templates, breaking autoescape=True on newer versions.' I read the actual installed starlette source (.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/starlette/templating.py, v0.52.1 per uv.lock) and confirmed `Jinja2Templates.__init__` now takes only `directory`, `context_processors`, and `env` as keyword args with no `**env_options` catch-all; when `directory` is given it hardcodes `autoescape=jinja2.select_autoescape()` (extension-based, not blanket True) and silently ignores any `autoescape=` kwarg passed in -- or, in the exact call shape used here, raises `TypeError: unexpected keyword argument 'autoescape'` outright. Either way, the explicit, version-independent autoescape guarantee the prior fix established is gone and now depends entirely on which Starlette version ends up installed. This matters because the project's Dockerfile does `pip install --no-cache-dir .` (unpinned, not `uv sync` against the lockfile), so the production image's Starlette version is not fixed to the one I verified -- a future image build could silently resolve a version where the `autoescape=True` kwarg is accepted without error but not actually applied uniformly (the original failure mode the reverted fix was written to close), re-enabling template auto-escaping gaps instead of failing loudly.
findings.title: Reverted Jinja2 autoescape fix reintroduces XSS exposure (and breaks startup on the pinned Starlette version)
findings.why_it_matters: Templates in triggarr/templates/partials/app_card.html and settings.html render user/config-controlled strings (instance names, app names, Radarr/Sonarr tag names) directly via `{{ ... }}` with no per-value `| safe` or manual escaping anywhere in the template set -- they rely entirely on the Jinja environment's autoescape setting for XSS protection. If an instance name or tag value containing `<script>` or an event handler attribute is ever rendered with autoescape not actually enabled, it executes in the dashboard viewer's browser. The previous fix existed specifically because the naive `Jinja2Templates(directory=..., autoescape=True)` call does not reliably enable escaping across Starlette versions; reverting to it reintroduces that exact, previously-identified failure mode.

findings.problem: Before this diff, autoescape=True was set directly on a jinja2.Environment the app built itself, so it held on every Starlette version. After it, autoescaping depends on Starlette accepting and forwarding `**env_options`. If the kwarg were silently dropped, or the code changed to `directory=` alone, the fallback is select_autoescape(), which escapes only .html/.htm/.xml templates. All 11 templates are .html today, so that fallback would still escape them, but nothing in the code guarantees it.
